title: Turn-segment validation at waypoint_tolerance 0.15 -- PASSED
purpose: Close the gap left by the 2026-08-08 slow-tier validation, which was deliberately turn-free. Gate 5 is an L-path and REQUIRES a turn, and Gate 4 turns were the ones that overshot.
key_findings: A segment requiring an 89.4 deg turn reached target within 0.1130 m -- inside the 0.15 m tolerance adopted in beta30. The turn path is now validated, not assumed.

Travel ratio 1.002 (0.8013 m for a 0.800 m path). The three pure-linear segments all UNDERSHOT (0.88-0.98); adding a turn brought it to essentially exact. Turning does not reintroduce the overshoot that 0.08 m caused.

Two realignments fired with aim errors of -25.3 and -32.4 deg, both resolving to target_heading_reached. Aim error GREW as the mower closed on the target (25 -> 32 deg), which is expected: a fixed cross-track offset subtends a larger angle at shorter range.
Both realignments stayed well under the 90 deg reverse-recovery threshold, so beta22 containment never fired. That is the designed behaviour, now observed rather than inferred.

VIO heading (99.09 deg) agreed with the independently measured travel heading (99.65 deg) to within 0.56 deg -- daylight VIO is trustworthy, and this is the VIO path, not the broken toward+offset path.

today_combined.note: Three pure-linear plus one 89.4 deg turn segment. Every one inside tolerance.

gate: armed immediately before, disarmed immediately after, verified both times
